# BLO-34510 — correct a comment that will become false when `secrets: update` is retired

Changed files:

- `src/server/execute.ts` — comment only, inside `createOrAdoptRunSecret`. No
  behaviour change; the call is still the merge `patchNamespacedSecret` that
  [BLO-32424](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/BLO/issues/BLO-32424) introduced.

## Why

That comment asserted *"That 403 is no longer live: #1837 added `update` to that
Role on 2026-09-16, and SSAR … now reports it allowed."* True when written, and
false the moment this PR lands — it removes `update` from
`deploy/helm/paperclip/templates/role.yaml`, because BLO-32424 converting this
very call site to a PATCH left the verb with no in-release-namespace consumer.

Worth the diff rather than leaving it: the next person here is someone
debugging a Secret 403 on the adopt path, and the stale version tells them the
verb is granted and the 403 must be something else. That is the exact failure
BLO-34510 was raised about — Ally's round-4 Important finding on #1873 was a
justification comment citing a call site that did not support it. Shipping the
retirement while leaving a second comment making the inverse claim would
reproduce it one file over.

The paragraph's *conclusion* was already right and is kept: this call stays a
PATCH. What changes is that it is now load-bearing rather than incidental —
`patch` was granted before #1837, which is what made the retirement safe, and
converting this back to a PUT would 403 on every collision again. The comment
now says that, and names the two files any such change would have to touch
(`role.yaml` and `role-rbac.test.mjs`, whose assertion is now inverted to pin
the verb's ABSENCE).

The sandbox-provider plugin's PUT in `secret-manager.ts` is still called out as
tenant-namespace, since it is the one in-tree Secret PUT left and the reason it
neither justified nor blocked the retirement. Its line-number citations were
dropped in favour of symbols — nothing about editing that plugin prompts anyone
to open this file, so a line number here rots silently.
